function: Multi-user CSI feedback: UE-side encoders and BS-side residual cross-attention transformer decoder with deep joint source-channel coding over a noisy uplink, reconstructing angle-delay CSI (pp. 2-3).
system: FDD massive MIMO-OFDM: BS with 32-antenna ULA, 2-4 single-antenna UEs, 1024 subcarriers truncated to 32, 6.7 GHz, UMa; AWGN uplink; no RIS (pp. 2-3).
method: Transformer encoder-decoder with residual cross-attention blocks at the BS, parameter sharing across UEs, DJSCC trained end-to-end with MSE; two-stage training: pretrain over SNRs, fine-tune per SNR (pp. 2-3).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa per 3GPP TR 38.901 UMa, 6.7 GHz, 4 correlated UEs in 300 m x 300 m cell; 80,000 train, 20,000 validation, 10,000 test samples (p. 3).
test_conditions: Held-out test split of one QuaDRiGa UMa scenario; sweeps over compression ratio, uplink SNR (0-20 dB) and 1-4 UEs; UE count used in training not stated (pp. 3-5).
baselines: Non-learned: CDL-OP, a dictionary-based CS method, noise-free. Learned: BL2 ADJSCC-CSINet+ [11], BL3 with fusion of [10]; own variants BL1, BL4, BL5 and SSCC with LDPC and QAM (pp. 4-5).
metrics: Average reconstruction NMSE in dB per UE (Table I, Figs. 3-4); FLOPs and parameters (Table II) (pp. 3-5).
complexity: Table II: Ours 2 UEs 289.83 M FLOPs and 5.55 M parameters; Ours 4 UEs 579.66 M FLOPs, 5.55 M; BL1, BL2 and BL3 also listed (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 3: "The downlink CSI dataset is generated by QuaDRiGa [17] in accordance with the 3GPP TR 38.901 [16]"; the UMa scenario at 6.7 GHz is used, so the model is trained and tested on a QuaDRiGa dataset of 3GPP TR 38.901.
q2_support: p. 3: "The training, validation and testing datasets consists of 80,000, 20,000, and 10,000 samples, respectively"; the test data are a held-out split of one dataset. p. 5: "we extend the numbers of UE of Ours to 3 and 4", but the paper does not say whether the network was trained with 2 UEs or retrained, and the CR and SNR sweeps do not count.
q3_support: p. 4: "significantly outperform the noise-free CDL-OP"; CDL-OP is the dictionary-based CS method that the paper calls conventional. p. 4: "BL2 is the DJSCC-based single-user CSI feedback proposed in [11], named ADJSCC-CSINet+"; both comparisons are on NMSE (Table I).
q4_support: p. 4: "we calculate the floating-point operations (FLOPs) and parameters of BL1, BL2, BL3, and Ours"; Table II gives 289.83 M FLOPs and 5.55 M parameters for Ours with 2 UEs.
q5_support: p. 3: "The downlink CSI dataset is generated by QuaDRiGa"; the authors generate their own dataset with a simulator, and no link, DOI or release statement for the code or the data appears in the paper.
notes: q3: the non-learned baseline is CDL-OP of [18], a dictionary-learning CS method that the paper calls a conventional CS-based approach and runs noise-free (p. 4), so the reviewer should confirm that it counts as non-learned; the learned baselines are BL2 (ADJSCC-CSINet+ of [11]) and BL3 (fusion branches of [10]) (p. 4). q2: the CR, SNR and number-of-UEs results (Table I, Figs. 3 and 4) are not shown to be tests outside the training conditions; if the reviewer reads Fig. 3 (p. 5) as a model trained with fewer UEs and tested with more, q2 would be 1. q5: QuaDRiGa generates the dataset but no release is stated. The PDF is arXiv 2505.19465v1 of 26 May 2025 and prints no DOI; its title and first authors match the Crossref record of the DOI.
